steps.title: Look at the two groups of verbs.
steps.prompt: What is different about the second group?
options: The verbs do not change at all.
The past form does not use -ed.
The verbs are only for he and she.
steps.answer: The past form does not use -ed.
steps.why: These are irregular verbs. You have to learn each past form.
steps.html:
work → worked · call → called · wait → waited

go → went · take → took · buy → bought

steps.title: Past Simple · irregular verbs
steps.html:
VerbPastExample
gowentI went to the shops.
havehadWe had a nice evening.
getgotShe got home at ten.
seesawI saw a good film.
buyboughtHe bought a coffee.

There is no rule. The past form of an irregular verb must be learned.

The form is the same for every person: I went, she went, they went.

After didn't, irregular verbs go back to the base form too: I didn't go.

Learners often write goed or buyed. Those forms do not exist.

Negatives and questions in the past come in Lesson 4.

steps.title: Look at the title: 'The day it all went wrong'.
steps.sub: What do you think the three people write about?

options.label: Three days when they had problems

steps.title: The day it all went wrong
steps.html:
Marta. First, I got up late. Then I couldn't find my keys, so I left the flat through the window. My neighbour saw me and called the police. In the end I was two hours late for work — and the keys were in my coat.

Ivan. I bought a cake for my wife's birthday and took the bus home. I met a friend on the bus and we talked and talked. After that I went home — but the cake stayed on the bus. My wife said it was the funniest present of her life.

Chen. My first day at a new job. I made coffee for everybody, wrote my name on the board and gave a short talk. Everyone was very quiet. Then a man came in and told me the truth: I was in the wrong building.
